What cannot be lent out he copies by hand, a page or two a night, so that there is a second one — and twice now the Library has filed his copy as the original and nobody has corrected it.

cards.name: The Harbour Office
cards.text: Requires Willow and a Civics Character. Gain 2 Supply, and your opponent chooses: lose 2 Supply, or put a card from their hand on top of their deck.

options.label: Put a card back on top of your deck

cards.flavor: Willow started at nineteen with one bad ferry on terms its previous owner described for years as generous of him. She has been writing the terms herself ever since, and they are always two things, and one of them is always the one you did not want to be asked.

cards.name: The Cider Social
cards.text: Requires Quill and an Agriculture Character. Gain 2 Supply, then feed a Character costing 2 or less in your Unemployment; it comes back to work Busy.
cards.flavor: September to February, in the barn, and the Hiring Hall sends whoever is quietly out of work. Quill hands them a basket without ever mentioning it. Rosabeth's garden takes the ones who have stopped getting up; the orchard takes everybody, all the time, so that nobody has to admit to anything.

cards.name: Reading Lanterns
cards.text: Requires a Lore Character. Limited 2: at the start of your turn, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Inkwell has the little ones one evening a week and tells them about the worlds on the other side of ours; Lynnette reads on Thursdays, on the floor, doing all the voices. The lanterns are Benjamin's, filled at his bench and nowhere else, and they are hung low enough for a mouse to read by.

cards.name: Tool Lending Day
cards.text: Requires Berry and a Crafts Character. Take a card costing 3 or less back out of your Town Dump into your hand, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Half the borough's broken things are queued along the bench and the other half are out on loan. Berry does not mend them for you. Berry puts the thing in your paws, sits on the second stool, and asks what you think is wrong with it, and is still asking an hour later when you have fixed it.

cards.name: The Root Cellar
cards.text: Requires an Agriculture Character. Rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Everything off Cookie's board is made to be opened in a different season from the one it was made in — hard biscuit, rusk, seed cake, baked on the late heat of the Community Oven after the bread is out. She dates the shelf in pencil and has never once been wrong about how long it would have to last.

cards.name: A Glut of Squash
cards.text: Requires two Agriculture Characters. Gain 4 Supply, then discard 1 card.
cards.flavor: Thistle set the pace down the row and never once looked back, and now there is more squash than the borough can eat and a grange meeting about it on Thursday. Quill has taken forty for the barn. Morty has taken sixty and will not say what for.

cards.name: The Seed Bank's Open Day
cards.text: Take an Agriculture token and draw 1 card. Then spend 2 Agriculture tokens: recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters upright.
cards.flavor: Every variety the First Boroughs have ever grown, dried, doubled and labelled, and one afternoon a year when Maribel puts the drawers out on the trestles. You do not pay for a packet. You come back next autumn with two of them, which she writes down, and that is the whole of the arrangement.

cards.name: The Town Clock
cards.text: Look at the top three cards of the Market Deck and put them back in any order, then your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: Brass gears, exposed on purpose, and a face the whole square sets its morning by. When it stops the borough calls Berry, and Berry answers to the Town Workshop about it afterwards, and the one thing everybody agrees on is that the hour it strikes is the hour it is.

cards.name: The Market Committee
cards.text: Your opponent chooses: you gain 3 Supply, or you look at the top three cards of the Market Deck, put them back in any order, and draw 1 card.

options.label: Let them set the Capital City deck

cards.flavor: Hazel has run the guild hall twice and sits on the committee in the coat they closed the stall in, and the committee has learned to offer two things it can live with rather than one it cannot. The weathervane over the square is a cat. Nobody will say who paid for that.

cards.name: The Fitting
cards.text: Gain 1 Supply, and your challenges cost 2 less Supply until your next turn.
cards.flavor: You describe it badly, waving, and Faustus has the bolt down before you have finished. He will not make a thing for a room he is not going to be in, which is why the Auction House has stopped pretending that a Mayor who walks in wearing one of his has not already cost everybody a rung.

cards.name: The Toll Gate
cards.text: Gain 1 Supply, then your opponent chooses: lose 3 Supply, or one of their Characters is put back to work.

options.label: Put one of your Characters back to work

cards.flavor: The gate is the borough's, the tolls are the harbour office's, and the season Finn had the keeping of it is mentioned to nobody. Pay it or work it off: the board by the bar has said so since before anybody currently arguing about it was born.

cards.name: The Owl Post
cards.text: Take any card back out of your Town Dump into your hand.
cards.flavor: Hibiscus walks the round and Juniper carries what leaves the borough, and the two of them hand over at the sorting bench at five every morning. Nothing on that round has ever been lost. What has been thrown away is a different question, and the answer is that Hibiscus has it, and knew you would want it back.

cards.name: The Physic Garden
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may feed a Character costing 2 or less in your Unemployment; it comes back to work Busy.
cards.flavor: The Capital City built it to grow specimens and the borough uses it to grow animals. Rosabeth will not be drawn on the tinctures — the Science hall has twice failed to account for them — but she is perfectly clear about the rest of it: you are not here to be mended, you are here because the beds want doing.

cards.name: The Weighbridge
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Every loaded cart in or out of the borough crosses Liz's plate and is paid on what she writes. Copper's office certifies the bridge each spring and has never once had to adjust it, which Copper mentions every spring, and Liz has never once looked up.

cards.name: The Counting House
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: It budgets for Brett a year ahead and has stopped querying Tuppence's prices, and both of those are Orien's doing: he feeds the shift returns and the auction prices into an engine built out of Observatory cast-offs, and the figure comes back within a Supply.

cards.name: The Town Workshop
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply. Each of your Events needs one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: It keeps the jigs, the loan book and the standing argument about whether Moss's bench jig counts as the Workshop's now that half the borough uses it. Berry answers to this room when the clock stops and has never once been asked to explain anything else.

cards.name: Six Weeks Shut
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors lose 2 Supply, then each Mayor may rehire one Character from their Unemployment for free; it enters upright. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The winter the Grain Exchange shut is one of the borough's two reference points for a bad season. Copper did not open the cellar. He lent the salt out on the quiet instead, said there would be worse, and every animal who was put back to work that February was put back by a neighbour.

cards.name: The Bridge Goes
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors lose 2 Supply, and at each Mayor's next Ready their Characters do not advance. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The other reference point, and the spring Adam kept the carts moving the long way round rather than let the borough stop. It cost a day on every load and he has never claimed it as anything. The year the bridge went is how animals here date things.

cards.name: The Eclipse
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors draw 1 card, and at each Mayor's next Ready their Characters do not advance. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Sage had the time of it to the minute eleven months out and told anybody who would stand still. Nothing in the borough was done between the quarter hour either side of it, and Jessica's whole night class was out on the hill with smoked glass, which is the sort of homework she does set.

cards.name: The Meteor Shower
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors draw 1 card and gain 1 Supply. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Taco's cart moves up to the top of the hill for it, which is the only night of the year anybody can say in advance where the cart will be. Sage counts them aloud. Juniper, who settles even calls by going outside and looking up, has never missed one.

cards.name: The Full Moon
cards.text: On reveal: the Mayor with fewer Statues readies a Character and gains 2 Supply. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The night round needs no lanterns and Benjamin fills them anyway, on the grounds that a rule kept only on the nights it is needed is not a rule. Hoot knocks the waking list an hour early. Everything in the borough that has been waiting for light gets done between midnight and four.

cards.name: The Cutting Comes Down
cards.text: On reveal: every shift in progress in both towns ends at once and produces nothing, and at each Mayor's next Ready their Characters do not advance. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The long pull to the county gate is a quarter-hour shorter than the road it replaced, which was Adam's idea, and the cutting that made it shorter is the cutting that came down. He was up there with a lamp before the noise had finished and did not ask anybody to come with him.

cards.name: A Plague of Midges
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor draws 1 card, then discards down to 4 cards in hand. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Three days off the water and nothing whatever to be done about it. Bella filed a note on the hatch, cited twice since; Rosabeth sold out of the green tincture by the second morning and gave the rest away; and every meeting in the borough that week was held with the door shut and got through in half the time.

cards.name: A Lean Season
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor sends one Character of their choice to Unemployment. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Not a disaster. A season in which there is simply nothing on, and the Hiring Hall's board is bare by Tuesday. Quinn turns back four years, finds the animals who did that exact work in the last one and has not been asked since, and starts handing out slips with names on them.

cards.name: The Chit Press
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Crafts Character, take a Building token. Spend 3 Building tokens: draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: The ferry's family struck their own fare chits seven generations ago and everything the borough has stamped since is a copy of them, off Lynnette's press, in the same hard wood.

cards.name: Gwen's Counter
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the end of your turn, if you control a Food Character, take a Food token. At the start of your turn, spend 2 Food tokens: rehire a Character costing 2 or less from your Unemployment for nothing.
cards.flavor: A griddle, a hatch, a row of stools and an apron on a hook by the door. The Hiring Hall has twice asked to make it a formal arrangement and twice been told it would ruin it.

cards.name: The Puppet Booth
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the end of your turn, if you control an Entertainment Character, take an Entertainment token. At the start of your turn, spend 1 Entertainment token: draw a card.
cards.flavor: It folds flat and goes home on Gabe's back, and it has stood in the children's corner, the bakery queue and every late room Cassadee has ever given away.

cards.name: Never Handed Back
cards.text: Requires an Otter. Take 2 Otter tokens, then spend 3 Otter tokens: gain 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: A worn wooden otter on a round of hard wood, handed over at one bank and counted back at the other. Half the borough has one in a pocket it never handed back, and every one of them is still good.

cards.name: The Hat Goes Round
cards.text: Requires an Entertainment Character. Take an Entertainment token, then spend 3 Entertainment tokens: ready one of your Characters and gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Nobody has ever been paid more than the hat in that room and nobody has ever asked to be. It goes round at the end, it comes back heavier than the set was worth, and Cassadee puts the chairs away.

cards.name: The Marks Are Struck
cards.text: Requires a Crafts Character and a Civics Character. Take 2 Building tokens and draw a card.
cards.flavor: The building mark is struck twice a year and the consents are read aloud over the top of it, slowly, all of them. Velvet genuinely enjoys this and said so in a public meeting.

cards.name: Gwen
cards.title: Anybody's Counter
cards.text: Upgrades Gwen. Busy: give a shift to a Character out of work in your town, or to hired help lying in the City Dump, for 1 less Supply. They arrive upright.
cards.flavor: The Hiring Hall's board is across the square and Gwen has never once looked at it. Anybody who walks in and asks for work gets an apron, that day, and no questions about why they are not doing whatever it is the borough thinks they do.

cards.name: Gwen
cards.title: The Apron on the Hook
cards.text: Upgrades Gwen. Busy: give a shift to a Character out of work in either town, or to hired help lying in the City Dump, for 2 less Supply. They arrive upright.
cards.flavor: She pays at the end of the shift, in coin, and if you come back the next day she puts you on again. It has never mattered to her whose books you were on when you walked in, and she has never asked Ned to write any of it down.

cards.name: Oatmeal's Awning
cards.text: Requires Oatmeal. Gain 2 Supply. Each Mayor chooses one of their own Characters; until that Mayor’s second turn from now, nothing may take the chosen Character out of their town — not a rival, and not the weather.
cards.flavor: He is the oldest of nine and it shows in everything he does: he counts heads at the door, and the head count does not stop at the ward boundary. The rival Mayor gets an animal under the awning too, which Oatmeal regards as the whole point and the ward office regards as a filing problem.

cards.name: The Long Awning
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: Whenever any Character is sent to Unemployment, gain 2 Supply, and each Mayor chooses one of their own Characters; until that Mayor’s next turn, nothing may take the chosen Character out of their town.
cards.flavor: Oatmeal got the ward office to run it the length of the square the spring the yards went short, and the households that came through that spring unbothered were the ones he got to first. It has never been taken down.

cards.name: Willow
cards.title: The Harbour Office
cards.text: Busy, pay 10 Supply: send a Character of your rival’s to Unemployment.
cards.flavor: She started with one ferry and terms the previous owner described for years afterwards as generous of him. She sells big, she has never in her life sold anybody a small thing, and the price for an animal’s contract is the price whether you like hearing it or not.

cards.name: Pockets
cards.title: A Quiet Arrangement
cards.text: Upgrades Pockets. Busy, pay 7 Supply: send a Character of your rival’s costing 2 or less to Unemployment.
cards.flavor: Nothing he does is quite a crime. Several things he does are the shape of one, seen from a distance, in poor light — and the animal who is suddenly not on the rival’s books this morning is not a thing Pockets said he did.

cards.name: Liz
cards.title: The Docket
cards.text: Upgrades Liz. Busy, pay 4 Supply: until the end of your turn, every card in the Capital City costs you 3 less.
cards.flavor: Every loaded cart in or out of the borough’s biggest building crosses her plate, and what she writes on the docket is what everybody after her is paid on. She reads the carter’s face while the beam is settling and has never once needed to do anything about it.

cards.name: Liz
cards.title: Chief Assessor
cards.text: Upgrades Liz. Busy, pay 5 Supply: until the end of your turn, Statues cost you 7 less.
cards.flavor: Copper’s office certifies the weighbridge every spring and has never once had to adjust it, which is how a Fox who reads faces ended up the animal the quarry cannot argue with. She reads the number out once.

cards.name: Ned
cards.title: The Ward Roll
cards.text: Busy, pay 6 Supply: search your deck for a Character, take it into your hand, then shuffle.
cards.flavor: Every ward roll, every guild return, every name on the hiring list since before Ned was born — filed, cross-referenced and correct, because a record that is nearly correct is a record that will one day be quoted by somebody who is nearly wrong.

cards.name: Scott
cards.title: The Index
cards.text: Upgrades Scott. Busy, pay 4 Supply: search your deck for an Event, take it into your hand, then shuffle.
cards.flavor: He has worked out over a long career exactly where in a ward-boundary dispute to put a joke about somebody’s uncle, and he can find the dispute, the uncle and the joke in under a minute, because he indexed all three.

cards.name: Sage
cards.title: The Watch List
cards.text: Upgrades Sage. Busy: look at the top three cards of the Market Deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: Sage keeps the borough’s watch list — what is due, what is late, what has not been seen since a year nobody here was alive for — and keeps it to the minute. The Capital City’s dealing order is a much smaller sky and holds no mysteries at all.

cards.name: Andrew
cards.title: The Late Desk
cards.text: Upgrades Andrew. Busy: look at the top two cards of the Market Deck and put one of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: He locks up after Inkwell’s evening and does not go home. What cannot be lent out he copies by hand, a page or two a night — and a thing filed at the back of the drawer at two in the morning is not seen again for a very long time.

cards.name: Bean
cards.title: The Early Shift
cards.text: Upgrades Bean. Busy, pay 2 Supply: look at the top three cards of the Market Deck and put one of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: They open before the early shift and are still wiping down when the night workers come off, and in between they hear the whole borough say what it is going to bid on before it has said so to anybody who matters.

cards.name: Jessica
cards.title: The Night School
cards.text: Upgrades Jessica. At the start of your turn, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: The animals who turn up at the night school are not kittens; they are animals already doing a job who have worked out that they need one more thing. Jessica teaches them what is coming up at the Auction House as a round with actions.

cards.name: The Short Week
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor lets one of their own Characters go to Unemployment, choosing for themselves. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Four days on the board instead of six, posted at the Hiring Hall without comment. Gwen’s counter is busy by nine and Bean’s is busy by ten, and neither of them mentions why.

cards.name: The Hiring Freeze
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor lets two of their own Characters costing 1 or less go to Unemployment, choosing for themselves. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The Capital City stops signing, and the first names off any board are the ones who have been on it the shortest. Quill’s orchard takes everybody, all the time, so that nobody has to admit to anything.

cards.name: The Yards Go Quiet
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor lets one of their own Characters costing 3 or less go to Unemployment, choosing for themselves, and then draws a card. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: No order comes down and nothing is announced. The stone stops arriving, the sheds are swept out twice in a week for want of anything else to do, and everybody reads the notice board rather harder than usual.

cards.name: The Redundancy Notice
cards.text: On gain: send a Character of your rival’s costing 3 or less to Unemployment.
cards.flavor: A single sheet, correctly worded, served at the end of the shift so that nobody has to stand about afterwards. Ned holds that the wording is the only kind thing about it and will not be argued out of the position.

cards.name: The Last Round
cards.text: On gain: each Mayor lets one of their own Characters go to Unemployment, choosing for themselves, and then gains 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: The books are squared, the last wages are paid out in full and in coin, and everybody is walked to the door rather than left to find it. Oatmeal insists on that part and has never once had to ask twice.

cards.name: Tuppence
cards.title: Sold Before the Cart
cards.text: Upgrades Tuppence. Busy: your next announcement in the Capital City cannot be raised against.
cards.flavor: They buy ahead of the borough’s understanding — the fittings, the stuff, the odd modern material nobody here has a use for yet — which means the lot is spoken for before the rest of the square has worked out what it is.

cards.name: A Word Beforehand
cards.text: Requires a Commerce Character. Your next announcement in the Capital City cannot be raised against.
cards.flavor: Earl has the long afternoons, when an animal who needs to sit down with somebody for two hours comes and sits down with somebody for two hours. A good deal of the Auction House is settled over the second pot.

cards.name: Taco
cards.title: The Four O’Clock Cart
cards.text: Upgrades Taco. Busy: gain 5 Supply. Your Characters do not advance at your next Ready phase.
cards.flavor: Lightermen come off a boat at four in the morning wanting something hot and Taco is there with it. The town that ate at four in the morning is not, on the whole, up at eight.

cards.name: The Long Night at Earl's
cards.text: Requires a Food Character. Draw three cards. Your Characters do not advance at your next Ready phase.
cards.flavor: There are two Earls and the difference between them is a pot of tea. The one who is still pouring at two in the morning has heard everything worth hearing in the borough and is in no state to be anywhere at nine.

cards.name: Annabelle
cards.title: Last One Up
cards.text: Upgrades Annabelle. At the start of your turn, if she is the only Raccoon you have standing, gain 2 Supply and draw a card.
cards.flavor: She pulls the paper out before the weather gets at it, and the hour that is good for that is the hour when the Salvage Yard has nobody else in it. What is legible she flattens, dries and files; what is not she keeps anyway.

cards.name: Cassadee
cards.title: The Only One at the Back
cards.job: The Only One at the Back
cards.text: Upgrades Cassadee. Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, if she is the only Hedgehog you have standing, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: She books it, sweeps it, sets the chairs, finds the lamp oil, stands at the back with the list, and puts the chairs away again at midnight. Nobody has ever been asked to help and nobody has ever quite worked out that they could offer.

cards.name: Morty
cards.title: The Boiler Test
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you have raised two or more Buildings, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: The boiler test is an annual embarrassment that the whole borough attends and nothing has ever gone wrong at it, which Morty regards as the point and everybody else regards as a shame. A town with something standing in it is a town that has him in and out all week.

cards.name: The Builders' Rest
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you have raised two or more Buildings, draw a card and gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Two benches, a tap and a roof, put up by Moss on the third job on the grounds that there had now been three. Barrow costed it, disapproved of it in writing, and eats his lunch in it.

cards.name: Peter
cards.title: The Winter's Length
cards.text: Upgrades Peter. Whenever one of your Characters begins a shift, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: It takes a winter to do a field’s length and about fifteen years to find out whether you did it properly. Peter is the reason the borough’s hedges are harder to take down than they look, and he is paid at the start of the work because that is when the work is.

cards.name: The Muster Bell
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: Once each turn, when one of your Characters begins a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Rung once at the top of the shift and never for anything else, which is why the borough can tell the time by it and why Adam will not have it rung for a road closure.

cards.name: Beck
cards.title: The Relief Roll
cards.text: Whenever any Character is sent to Unemployment, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: He clerks — bylaws, ward rolls, the lamplighters’ hours — and he clerks well, because the work is quiet and nobody needs him to be interesting at it. The relief roll is the one page of it he keeps in his own hand.

cards.name: Works in the Square
cards.title: Capital City Ordinance
cards.text: While this is displayed, no Statue may be bought. Either Mayor may put an upright Character to work clearing the square; when two have been put to work, between them or by one Mayor alone, the works finish and this leaves the Capital City.
cards.flavor: Adam has the square up for the cobbles and will not be hurried about it. The quarry carts stand at the top of the lane for a fortnight and the Capital City discovers it has nowhere to put a monument.

cards.name: The Quarry Road Is Out
cards.title: Capital City Ordinance
cards.text: While this is displayed, no Statue may be bought. Either Mayor may put an upright Character to work on the road; when three have been put to work, between them or by one Mayor alone, it opens again and this leaves the Capital City.
cards.flavor: The long pull up to the county gate went in the wet, and Adam was out on it the year the bridge went and is out on it again. Nothing carved comes down that road until it is made, and everybody knew that before they started arguing.

cards.name: Monument Tax
cards.title: Capital City Ordinance
cards.text: While this is displayed, Statues cost 4 more.
cards.flavor: The Capital City would like it minuted that a borough rich enough to raise a monument is a borough rich enough to be asked about it. Copper read the schedule twice, said “we’ll see”, and put more by.

cards.name: The Masons' Rate
cards.title: Capital City Ordinance
cards.text: While this is displayed, Statues cost 3 less.
cards.flavor: The quarry has more stone cut than it has orders for, and Barrow has costed the difference on the back of a docket and posted it where the two Mayors will both walk past it.

cards.name: The Timber Levy
cards.title: Capital City Ordinance
cards.text: While this is displayed, Buildings in the Capital City cost 3 more.
cards.flavor: The cutting came down and the price of a roof went up the same week, which Moss says is a coincidence and Barrow says is the oldest arrangement in the trade.

cards.name: The Building Grant
cards.title: Capital City Ordinance
cards.text: While this is displayed, Buildings in the Capital City cost 2 less.
cards.flavor: Voted through at a ward meeting Quinn was at the back of with the book open. It is worded so plainly that the Counting House has read it four times looking for the catch.

cards.name: The Sealed Bid
cards.title: Capital City Ordinance
cards.text: While this is displayed, no auction in the Capital City may be raised against.
cards.flavor: One bid, in writing, in a box, opened at the hour. Faustus loathes it, on the grounds that there is nothing in it for anybody to watch, and has said so at length to a room that agreed with him and kept the box.

cards.name: A Word With the Steward
cards.title: Capital City Ordinance
cards.text: While this is displayed, no auction in the Capital City may be raised against. Either Mayor may put an upright Character to work on the steward; when two have been put to work, between them or by one Mayor alone, the room opens again and this leaves the Capital City.
cards.flavor: The steward has views about calling out over a lot and has had them since before either Mayor was in office. He is not unreasonable; he is simply going to need a long afternoon and somebody to have it with.

cards.name: The Great Frost
cards.text: On reveal: every Character in both towns is sent to Unemployment. Each Mayor then rehires up to four of them for nothing, upright, and gains 2 Supply. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The river went hard from the ferry steps to the county line and nothing was carried anywhere for five weeks. What the borough had put by came out of Copper’s cellar, in order, which is the only reason anybody remembers the frost fondly.

cards.name: The Year It Stopped
cards.text: On reveal: every Character in both towns is sent to Unemployment. Each Mayor then rehires up to four of them for nothing, upright, and draws a card. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Ned can give you the date, the order the boards came down in, and the morning each one went back up. Everybody else remembers it as the year the square was quiet and the reading room was full.

cards.name: The Small Fair
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor pays 8 Supply, or everything they have and Busies one Character. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Three stalls and a rope ring, but the toll man stands at the gate all the same. Copper says a fair this size is really just practice for the big one.

cards.name: The County Fair
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor pays 14 Supply, or everything they have and Busies one Character. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Every stall in the borough turns up at once, and every one of them wants paying. Nobody remembers who first called it a fair rather than a tax.

cards.name: The Assessor's Round
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor loses 25% of their Supply, rounded to the nearest whole number.
cards.flavor: The clipboards again, but this time they do not ask what you have put by; they can see it from the doorway and take their share off the top.

cards.name: The Reckoning
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor loses half their Supply, rounded to the nearest whole number.
cards.flavor: Copper keeps a second ledger for years like this one. He says it is not that the borough takes more from the rich; it is that the rich have more for the borough to take.

cards.name: The Midsummer Fair
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor pays 26 Supply, or everything they have and Busies one Character. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The longest day of the year and the longest queue at the gate. Whoever set the toll knew exactly how much a season of good trading leaves sitting in a strongbox.

cards.name: The Lord Mayor's Fair
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor pays 32 Supply, or everything they have and Busies one Character. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Once a generation, and the whole borough turns out, which is exactly the trouble: everyone with anything put by is expected to put it in the box at the gate.

cards.name: Tabitha
cards.title: Festival Photographer
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: She borrowed the camera for one afternoon at the Festival Green. Nobody has seen it go back.

cards.name: Tabitha
cards.title: Lens Apprentice
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Sota showed her the bench, not the sky. She has never once looked through an eyepiece the right way round on the first try, and never the second time either.

cards.name: Tabitha
cards.title: Videographer
cards.text: Upgrades Tabitha. When Tabitha becomes upright, put one of your opponent's Characters back to work.
cards.flavor: She calls it getting the reaction shot. Nobody in the other town remembers agreeing to be in the scene.

cards.name: Tabitha
cards.title: Optics Scientist
cards.text: Upgrades Tabitha. When Tabitha becomes upright, put one of your opponent's Characters back to work, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: She finally knows exactly how the thing in her hands works, which means she also knows precisely which of the other town's cameras is about to jam.

cards.name: Tabitha
cards.title: Camerawoman
cards.text: Upgrades Tabitha. When Tabitha becomes upright, put up to 2 of your opponent's Characters back to work.
cards.flavor: The dream was never the photograph. It was the moment before it, when everyone in frame does exactly what she needs them to.

cards.name: Abigail
cards.title: Counter Girl
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: She has the whole counter's order in her head before the first plate goes down.

cards.name: Abigail
cards.title: Five Minutes on a Slow Night
cards.text: A shift: 1 turn, 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: Cassadee gave her the slot on nothing at all. Abigail has never once given her a reason to take it back.

cards.name: Abigail
cards.title: Gwen's Best Waitress
cards.text: A shift: 2 turns, 5 Supply.
cards.flavor: The jar by the register has her name on it more often than the register does.

cards.name: Abigail
cards.title: The Standing Slot
cards.text: A shift: 2 turns, 6 Supply.
cards.flavor: She is never going to be the thing the room remembers about that night. She goes anyway, on her feet after a full shift.

cards.name: Winter
cards.title: Segment Runner
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: He plans the running order the night before, then again in the morning, then once more on the walk over.

cards.name: Winter
cards.title: Turned-Down Applicant
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Two courteous letters, no seat. He kept the letters and everything he read for the second one.

cards.name: Winter
cards.title: Science Show Host
cards.text: Upgrades Winter. Busy: look at the top 2 cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: He reads the Capital City's stalls the way he reads a running order: what's coming up, and in what order it should arrive.

cards.name: Winter
cards.title: Head Science Producer
cards.text: Upgrades Winter. When Winter becomes upright, look at the top 2 cards of the Market Deck and put them back in whichever order you choose.
cards.flavor: The manifests, the order book, the launch windows — none of it was wasted. It just found a different desk.

cards.name: Winter
cards.title: Everyone's Favorite TV Scientist
cards.text: Upgrades Winter. While Winter is upright, the Capital City deals one extra stall.
cards.flavor: He wanted a sixth stall in the Capital City so the show would always have one more thing to point at. Now there is one, and it is his.

cards.name: Fred
cards.title: Wandered Onto the Stage
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: He says he was looking for the toilets. The borough has decided to believe him.

cards.name: Fred
cards.title: Held the Ladder Wrong
cards.text: Upgrades Fred. Busy: toss a coin. Heads, gain 2 Supply. Tails, your opponent gains 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Benjamin has never worked out whose side he was on. Neither has Fred.

cards.name: Fred
cards.title: Backstage Crew (Nobody Asked)
cards.text: A shift: 2 turns, 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: He was never told the name of the show. He still hasn't asked.

cards.name: Fred
cards.title: The Crew Doesn't Ask Anymore
cards.text: Upgrades Fred. When Fred becomes upright, toss a coin. Heads, gain 2 Supply and draw a card. Tails, your opponent gains 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Roger has twice asked him to be the one who calls the ha'penny in the air. Fred has twice said that even that felt like too much responsibility.

cards.name: Yellow
cards.title: Open Mic Regular
cards.text: When Yellow is recruited, Yellow cannot be targeted by an opponent's effect until your next turn.
cards.flavor: He rolled into town telling everyone how fresh his rhymes were. Nobody has managed to argue him out of a slot since.

cards.name: Yellow
cards.title: Freshest Thing in a Small Town
cards.text: Upgrades Yellow. Yellow cannot be sent to Unemployment.
cards.flavor: Whatever else is true about the rhymes, the Hiring Hall has never once had cause to wonder where he is. Now it never will.

cards.name: Yellow
cards.title: Rapper
cards.text: Upgrades Yellow. A long shift: 2 turns, 5 Supply. Yellow cannot be sent to Unemployment. When Yellow is recruited, another Character you control cannot be targeted by an opponent until your turn after next. At the start of your turn, draw 1 card and gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The suburbs record is finished, it is forty minutes long, and side two is entirely about the seed bank. Cassadee has stopped trying to cut anything from the set and the hall sells out anyway, which Yellow has been saying would happen since the week he arrived.

cards.name: Bunny
cards.title: Kit
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Rabbit costing more than 1 may be played over Bunny as an upgrade, and pays as though Bunny cost 1.
cards.flavor: Clover gave one a row of its own the summer the beds went in, and by August there were nine rows and no way of saying which Bunny had which.

cards.name: Baby Mouse
cards.title: Pup
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Mouse costing more than 2 may be played over Baby Mouse as an upgrade, and pays as though Baby Mouse cost 2.
cards.flavor: Lynnette found the missing year of Grain Exchange returns behind the atlases. Lynnette did not find them. A Baby Mouse found them and Lynnette carried them.

cards.name: Badger Cub
cards.title: Cub
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Badger costing more than 2 may be played over Badger Cub as an upgrade, and pays as though Badger Cub cost 2.
cards.flavor: Barrow's first block is still on the shelf above his bench. It is not a good block. He will not have it moved.

cards.name: Hoglet
cards.title: Hoglet
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Hedgehog costing more than 1 may be played over Hoglet as an upgrade, and pays as though Hoglet cost 1.
cards.flavor: Bristle let one hold the gate for an afternoon as a joke. Two carters and a Fox turned round and came back with their paperwork.

cards.name: Raccoon Kit
cards.title: Kit
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Raccoon costing more than 2 may be played over Raccoon Kit as an upgrade, and pays as though Raccoon Kit cost 2.
cards.flavor: Pockets gave one a ha'penny for a doorknob with no door. It is still on the shelf. It is still, Pockets maintains, worth a ha'penny.

cards.name: Fox Cub
cards.title: Cub
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Fox costing more than 2 may be played over Fox Cub as an upgrade, and pays as though Fox Cub cost 2.
cards.flavor: A Cub on the steps called the timber lot four rungs before the room did, to nobody, and has been insufferable ever since.

cards.name: Otter Pup
cards.title: Pup
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Otter costing more than 1 may be played over Otter Pup as an upgrade, and pays as though Otter Pup cost 1.
cards.flavor: Dylan carried one across the counter on a tray and both of them behaved as though that were the ordinary way to cross a room.

cards.name: Squirrel Kit
cards.title: Kit
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Squirrel costing more than 1 may be played over Squirrel Kit as an upgrade, and pays as though Squirrel Kit cost 1.
cards.flavor: Peanut's first tin is in the café office with the year scratched on the lid. It has four acorns in it. It has had four acorns in it since.

cards.name: Kitten
cards.title: Kitten
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Cat costing more than 1 may be played over Kitten as an upgrade, and pays as though Kitten cost 1.
cards.flavor: Marmalade sends the front row home with buns. The buns do not reach the front row's homes and Marmalade has never asked about it.

cards.name: Owlet
cards.title: Owlet
cards.text: A very long shift: 3 turns, 1 Supply. Any Owl costing more than 2 may be played over Owlet as an upgrade, and pays as though Owlet cost 2.
cards.flavor: Mandee carries the lanterns and lets an Owlet hold the pole. The Owlet has never once dropped it, and has been told so exactly once.

cards.name: Shay
cards.title: Sunday Painter
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Green, mostly. She is aware it is mostly green. The trestle goes up at eight and the price card says what it says.

cards.name: Shay
cards.title: Ward Doctor
cards.text: Busy: one of your Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Two doors from the Physic Garden, a bell on a string, and a light on at the hours nobody else keeps a light on.

cards.name: Shay
cards.title: Borough Physician
cards.text: Upgrades Shay. Busy: one of your Characters and one of your opponent's Characters each turn one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: She does the round twice and the second round crosses the ward boundary. It has been raised at three meetings. It has never once been stopped.

cards.name: Shay
cards.title: Market-Stall Painter
cards.text: Upgrades Shay. When Shay finishes a shift, draw a card.
cards.flavor: Everything off the trestle by noon, and everything off the trestle turns into whatever came up on the late ferry addressed to nobody in particular.

cards.name: Shay
cards.title: Chief Physician
cards.text: Upgrades Shay. Busy: one of your Characters and one of your opponent's Characters each turn one step toward upright, then draw a card.
cards.flavor: Whatever is new, Shay read it the night it came. Whoever is unwell, Shay is already on the step. The borough has never worked out when she sleeps and has stopped asking in case she answers.

cards.name: JT
cards.title: Ward Nurse
cards.text: Busy: rehire a Character costing 1 or less from your Unemployment.
cards.flavor: He does the voice. It is not a good voice. The paw comes off the arm of the chair every single time.

cards.name: JT
cards.title: Children's Ward Nurse
cards.text: Upgrades JT. Busy: two of your Characters costing 1 or less each turn one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: The whole front row at once, which is the trick: nobody wants to be the one who is still sitting down when the others have got up.

cards.name: JT
cards.title: Juice List
cards.text: Upgrades JT. Busy: one of your Characters hands their shift to another.
cards.flavor: Clean shirt, three evenings a week. 'Now, the pears.' Nobody has yet escaped the pears.

cards.name: JT
cards.title: Juice Sommelier
cards.text: Upgrades JT. Busy: one of your Characters costing 4 or more is readied, and you gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: He pours for the top of the bill and he pours for the child at the next table, and he gives them the same thirty seconds about the pears. The child gets the better version.

cards.name: Reese
cards.title: Crop Duster
cards.text: Busy: take a Market card from the City Dump into your hand.
cards.flavor: Low over the far field at six in the morning, and Maribel has stopped waving because he has stopped being surprised by it.

cards.name: Reese
cards.title: Charter Pilot
cards.text: Upgrades Reese. Busy: draw 2 cards, then discard 1 card.
cards.flavor: The coat is yellow, it is August, and the passenger has not asked because the passenger has worked out that asking is the point.

cards.name: Reese
cards.title: Chief Pilot
cards.text: Upgrades Reese. Busy: take a Market card from the City Dump into your hand, then draw a card.
cards.flavor: He goes when the weather has shut the ferry and he tells it afterwards as though it were a short walk. He also read the freight notes out of the bin first, and that part he tells nobody.

cards.name: Dirt
cards.title: Classroom Assistant
cards.text: Busy: swap this card with Dirt or Squirt in your hand. The post is not lost and nothing is paid.
cards.flavor: On his first morning he was introduced to the upper room as Squirt, said nothing, and taught the whole term under it.

cards.name: Dirt
cards.title: Schoolteacher, Upper Room
cards.text: Upgrades Dirt. Busy: swap this card with Dirt or Squirt in your hand. The post is not lost and nothing is paid.
cards.flavor: He lets the wrong answer sit there. The room cannot stand it. Somebody always fixes it themselves, which is the entire method and he has never written it down.

cards.name: Dirt
cards.title: Figurine Painter
cards.text: Upgrades Dirt. Busy: swap this card with Dirt or Squirt in your hand. The post is not lost and nothing is paid. When Dirt finishes a shift, put 2 Supply by on him.
cards.flavor: An inch and a half tall, one a season, and the faces are right in a way that has made two animals in this borough quietly uncomfortable.

cards.name: Dirt
cards.title: Master Figuremaker
cards.text: Upgrades Dirt. Busy: swap this card with Dirt or Squirt in your hand. The post is not lost and nothing is paid. When Dirt finishes a shift, take every Supply your Characters have put by.
cards.flavor: Eleven on Ned's shelf, and the twelfth is labelled DIRT and is unmistakably Squirt. Four years now. He has never corrected it and he never will.

cards.name: Squirt
cards.title: Playground Monitor
cards.text: Busy: swap this card with Dirt or Squirt in your hand. The post is not lost and nothing is paid.
cards.flavor: Ten minutes into anything he has decided is boring, he starts it. Dirt has never once refused and has never once looked surprised.

cards.name: Squirt
cards.title: Schoolteacher, Lower Room
cards.text: Upgrades Squirt. Busy: swap this card with Dirt or Squirt in your hand. The post is not lost and nothing is paid.
cards.flavor: The lower room's afternoon is arranged around a five o'clock kick-off. The school has never formally admitted this and has never once changed it.

cards.name: Squirt
cards.title: Borough Eleven, Left Wing
cards.text: Upgrades Squirt. Busy: swap this card with Dirt or Squirt in your hand. The post is not lost and nothing is paid. When Squirt finishes a shift, one of your other Characters is readied.
cards.flavor: Twenty years on that wing. He stops being funny the moment he crosses the line, which is the thing about him that surprises the ward meetings.

cards.name: Squirt
cards.title: Club Captain
cards.text: Upgrades Squirt. Busy: swap this card with Dirt or Squirt in your hand. The post is not lost and nothing is paid. When Squirt finishes a shift, one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Teresa shouts and he does what she says. Sota says nothing and he does what they say. Asked how he tells them apart, he said: one of them is loud.

cards.name: Teresa
cards.title: Pepper Grower
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Far end of the Allotment Strip, an unreasonable number of varieties, and a hand-written card for each that nobody can read from the path.

cards.name: Teresa
cards.title: Touchline Coach
cards.text: Busy: one of your opponent's Characters is put back to work — and so is Teresa, again.
cards.flavor: WONDERFUL. THAT IS THE IDEA. GOOD LAD. The allotments can hear it and the allotments have stopped looking up.

cards.name: Teresa
cards.title: Pepper Stall
cards.text: Upgrades Teresa. Busy: take an Event from your Town Dump into your hand.
cards.flavor: She is quieter at the market. Not quiet. Quieter. The trestle is next to Shay's and the two of them have never once agreed about the pricing.

cards.name: Teresa
cards.title: Head Coach
cards.text: Upgrades Teresa. Busy: two of your opponent's Characters are put back to work, and Teresa is put back to work twice over.
cards.flavor: If she has asked more of you this week than last week that is not an accident, and she has asked more of herself than of any of you, which also is not.

cards.name: Teresa
cards.title: Coach of the Borough Eleven
cards.text: Upgrades Teresa. Busy: two of your opponent's Characters are put back to work and you draw a card. Teresa is put back to work twice over.
cards.flavor: The appeal against the ferry-day postponement ran to nine pages and was won on the second. Whatever she takes out of the side in a season she puts back twice, and she has never once said so out loud.

cards.name: Mimi
cards.title: Trolley Service
cards.text: Busy: swap this card with any other Mimi in your hand.
cards.flavor: Two hundred cups down a gangway eleven inches wider than the trolley, and not one of them has ever gone over.

cards.name: Mimi
cards.title: Safety Demonstration
cards.text: Busy: swap this card with any other Mimi in your hand.
cards.flavor: Nobody watches it. She does it exactly the same every time anyway, which is the difference between her and everybody who has ever said nobody watches it.

cards.name: Mimi
cards.title: Cabin Pressure Check
cards.text: Upgrades Mimi. Busy: swap this card with any other Mimi in your hand.
cards.flavor: The checklist is Reese's responsibility and the checklist is done by Mimi, and the two of them have never once discussed this arrangement.

cards.name: Mimi
cards.title: Seat 1A Welcome
cards.text: Upgrades Mimi. Busy: swap this card with any other Mimi in your hand. When Mimi finishes a shift, draw a card.
cards.flavor: A diverted landing, a broken latch, a passenger with strong feelings about the seat numbering: same smile, same sentence, already fixing it.

cards.name: Mimi
cards.title: Purser
cards.text: Upgrades Mimi. Busy: swap this card with any other Mimi in your hand. Then, if you control another Rabbit, recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free.
cards.flavor: Five jobs in a uniform designed to look like one, and the bill settled at the far end. Ask her about the beets and you will get the smile and nothing else.

cards.name: Mildred
cards.title: Counter Clerk
cards.text: A steady shift: 2 turns, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Forty-one years and not one error. The queue forms anyway. The queue has always formed anyway.

cards.name: Mildred
cards.title: Teller
cards.text: Upgrades Mildred. Every shift your opponent finishes pays 1 Supply less while Mildred is standing.
cards.flavor: Nothing is taken and nothing is refused. There is a form, the form is correct, and the form takes a while.

cards.name: Mildred
cards.title: Chief Teller
cards.text: Upgrades Mildred. Every shift your opponent finishes pays 1 Supply less while Mildred is standing.
cards.flavor: She will tell you, kindly, what you could bring in tomorrow that would let her say yes. Animals bring it. That is the part the borough forgets to mention.

cards.name: Mildred
cards.title: Branch Manager
cards.text: Upgrades Mildred. Every shift your opponent finishes pays 2 Supply less while Mildred is standing. Busy: rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: She says no to a Mayor exactly as she says it to anybody else. It is the most expensive habit in the First Boroughs and it is why the borough's money has never once gone missing.

cards.name: Hoot
cards.title: Night Kitchen
cards.text: Busy: one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: If you are going to knock at four in the morning you had better have something with you, and Hoot worked that out in the first week.

cards.name: Hoot
cards.title: Breakfast Bell
cards.text: Upgrades Hoot. At the start of your turn, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Doors, lamps, deliveries, the ward's keys, and now the bell — and the bell is the one nobody has ever complained about.

cards.name: Hoot
cards.title: Head of the Night Kitchen
cards.text: Upgrades Hoot. At the start of your turn, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright and you gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The list of everybody's names is still in the bag behind the door. It has what they take in the morning written next to it now, and Hoot has never had to look.

cards.name: Sota
cards.title: Touchline Assistant
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control Teresa, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: They took the job because the light is better on the touchline than over a blank, and have never offered the borough a second reason.

cards.name: Sota
cards.title: Assistant Coach
cards.text: Upgrades Sota. Busy: Sota stands up, once per game, even from the wrong side of upright.
cards.flavor: Teresa can be heard from the allotments. Sota moves two paces up the line and the whole back four moves with them, and nobody has ever seen the signal.

cards.name: Farmer's Market
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply for each of your upright Characters, up to 3.
cards.flavor: Trestles on the square from six, down by one. Teresa's peppers are at the far end next to Shay's paintings and the two of them have never agreed about the pricing. It pays what the borough brought, which on a thin week is nothing much and on a full one is the best morning of the month.

cards.name: The Bookstore
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, draw 1 card, then discard 1 card.
cards.flavor: Ned's overflow, priced by somebody else and sold by nobody in particular. You never leave with nothing and you never leave with room in the bag, which is why the shelf by the door is for what you have decided against on the way out.

cards.name: The Owlery
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control an Owl, you may recruit an Owl from your hand for free.
cards.flavor: Brick, tall, and warm at the top, and the Capital City built it as a post house. The Owls moved in the first winter and the post has been a side effect ever since. There has to be one of them up there already or the rest do not come: Hoot keeps the list, and Hoot has never had to look at it.

cards.name: The Bank
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may put 2 tokens of any kind across the counter to gain 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: Mildred's counter, and the only place in the First Boroughs that does not care what kind of chit you have brought it. Two is two. She will count them in front of you, slowly, and she will be right.

cards.name: The Game Store
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may pay 3 Supply to draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: Dice, boards, painted figures an inch and a half tall that are not Dirt's and are sold as though they were. Supply goes in over the counter and comes back out as something to do on a Tuesday, which the borough has decided is a fair rate.

cards.name: The Fast Food Joint
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: Your Masters are ready a turn sooner. At the start of your turn, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright and you gain 1 Supply. Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, toss a coin: tails, a Character of yours costing 1 or less goes to Unemployment.
cards.flavor: Open at all hours, out in under a minute, and the whole town suddenly has time it did not have. Nobody has worked a full season in it and nobody can say in advance whose last week it is. Marmalade has never said a word against the place, which from Marmalade is the loudest thing anybody has said about it.

cards.name: The Cheese Store
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Mouse, gain 2 Supply. At the start of your turn, if you control a Raccoon, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: A cold room, a marble slab and a queue of two species. The Mice buy it. The Raccoons are here for the rind bin round the back, which the shop has stopped pretending is not the main trade.

cards.name: The Juice Store
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 2 Supply, then toss a coin: heads, a Character of your opponent's is put back to work at random; tails, one of yours is.
cards.flavor: JT drew up the list and then went back to the restaurant, and the counter has been run ever since by whoever is nearest. Somebody is always back behind it. It is not always somebody who meant to be.

cards.name: The Gas Station
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, your opponent discards 1 card.
cards.flavor: Two pumps, a bell on the forecourt cable and a bin that is emptied hourly. Whatever the other town came in holding, some of it goes in that bin before they leave, and nobody has ever been able to say quite how.

cards.name: The Car Dealership
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply and your opponent loses 4 Supply; your opponent may then recruit a Character costing 2 or less from their hand for free.
cards.flavor: Bunting, a brass bell and a Fox on the forecourt. Nobody has ever walked off this lot poorer and emptier-pawed at the same time, which is the whole art of it: you are four Supply down and you are driving something home and you cannot decide how you feel.

cards.name: The Airport
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may recruit a Character from your hand for free; they enter upright, cannot be pledged in an auction, and go to Unemployment at the end of your turn.
cards.flavor: Reese's field, one strip and a windsock, and Mimi runs the whole of the rest of it. An animal off the morning aircraft is standing in your town by nine and gone by supper, and the borough has decided that a day is a day.

cards.name: The Car Show
cards.text: Requires a Fox and a Commerce Character. Each Mayor may recruit up to 2 Characters from their hand for free.
cards.flavor: Bunting across the square, the dealership's brass bell going all afternoon, and both boroughs walking home with something. It is the Fox on the forecourt who opens it and the ledger animals who make it add up, and nobody remembers agreeing to hold it on the same day as the market — but the other town turns out in numbers, every year, and that is rather the point of it.

cards.name: Passing Comets
cards.text: Requires a Science Character. Each Mayor searches their deck for up to 2 cards, shows them, takes them into hand and shuffles.
cards.flavor: Somebody with a chart says when, and by ten the whole square is out on its back looking up — which means everybody is also, quietly, going and fetching the one card they have been waiting on. Sage counts them aloud. Nobody has ever pretended not to have seen what the other town came back with, and half the borough's best trades have been agreed lying on the cobbles.

cards.name: The Community Bonfire
cards.text: Requires a Lore Character. Each Mayor draws 1 card. Then draw 1 more for each Lore Character in your town, up to 3.
cards.flavor: One night a year the borough burns the year's broken pallets on the far field and the animals who keep the records do the talking, because a bonfire is where this town has always done its remembering. Ned brings the ward book. Lynnette brings the water-stained novels nobody has wanted since the bridge went. The other town walks over the hill for it and is handed a chair, and everybody goes home knowing something they did not.

cards.name: Cheese Festival
cards.text: Requires a Badger and a Mouse. Gain 4 Supply and take an Event from your Town Dump into your hand.
cards.flavor: The cold room is emptied onto trestles for one weekend and the two species who actually care about it run the whole thing between them: the Badgers carry and the Mice do the paperwork, and the paperwork is why it has happened every year without fail since anybody can remember.

cards.name: Cindy
cards.title: Clerk of the Court
cards.text: When Cindy is recruited, look at your opponent's hand.
cards.flavor: Nobody told her the clerk was allowed to read the papers before the bench did. Nobody has told her since, either.

cards.name: Cindy
cards.title: Magistrate
cards.text: Upgrades Cindy. When Cindy becomes upright, one of your opponent's Characters is put back to work.
cards.flavor: The remark was made at nine and the yard was still waiting on it at half past. Cindy had not raised her voice once.

cards.name: Cindy
cards.title: Circuit Judge
cards.text: Upgrades Cindy. Your challenge bids win ties. When an opponent challenges one of your purchases, gain 2 Supply and look at their hand.
cards.flavor: Four wards, four benches, one window that shuts and three that do not. She hears the side she stopped believing in all the way to the end, every time, in every one of them.

cards.name: Cindy
cards.title: Justice of the Boroughs
cards.text: Upgrades Cindy. Your challenge bids win ties. At the start of your turn, look at your opponent's hand, then your opponent chooses: one of their Characters is put back to work, or they lose 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Both boroughs bring it to her now, which neither of them enjoys. She gives the losing side the choice of how it loses, listens to the answer, and writes that down too.

cards.name: Elvira
cards.title: Tea-Leaf Reader
cards.text: Busy: toss a coin. Heads, look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom; tails, look at the top card of your opponent's deck.
cards.flavor: A cup, a saucer and whatever is left in the bottom of it. Elvira has never once said she could not see anything.

cards.name: Elvira
cards.title: Fairground Booth
cards.text: Upgrades Elvira. When Elvira becomes upright, toss a coin. Heads, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck; tails, look at the top two cards of your opponent's deck.
cards.flavor: Sixpence a reading, a shilling if you want it written down, and a queue that starts before she does.

cards.name: Elvira
cards.title: Fortune Teller
cards.text: Upgrades Elvira. Whenever Supply is taken from you, gain 2 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: She told the ferry office there was danger on the water for a fortnight. There was no danger on the water for a fortnight. She still sat with the two of them who could not sleep for it.

cards.name: Elvira
cards.title: Reader of the Long Odds
cards.text: Upgrades Elvira. At the start of your turn, toss a coin. Heads, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck and put them back in any order; tails, look at the top two cards of your opponent's deck. Busy, once per game: Elvira stands straight back up.
cards.flavor: Water in the cellar on a Thursday, she said, and there was — three Thursdays later, which she counts and the cellar does not.

cards.name: Jim
cards.title: Gadget Blogger
cards.text: Busy: pay 1 Supply to draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Eleven hundred words on a shutter mechanism, posted at four in the morning, and the borough read all of it.

cards.name: Jim
cards.title: Hobby Programmer
cards.text: Upgrades Jim. Busy: pay 2 Supply to draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: Built out of what was in the bin behind the works, and better than the thing it was copying. He will tell you that too.

cards.name: Jim
cards.title: Early Adopter
cards.text: Upgrades Jim. At the start of your turn, you may pay 4 Supply to draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: Launch day, second in the queue, and the patch of pale fur on the left of his head is from the last one. He is not embarrassed about the candle.

cards.name: Jim
cards.title: FutureTech Fanboy
cards.text: Upgrades Jim. Busy: pay 2 Supply to draw 4 cards, then Jim goes to your Unemployment.
cards.flavor: Two nights on the pavement outside the FutureTech store for a thing he already owns a working version of. He is not at the yard on Thursday and everybody knew he would not be.

cards.name: Robbie
cards.title: Cub Reporter
cards.text: When Robbie is recruited, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: DOWN THE PLUGHOLE, on the drainage review. He laughed in the office for some time, alone.

cards.name: Robbie
cards.title: Columnist
cards.text: Upgrades Robbie. When Robbie becomes upright, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: A SPAN OF ATTENTION, on the bridge inquiry. Four sheets and a Thursday, and the ward hall reads every one of them.

cards.name: Robbie
cards.title: Features Writer
cards.text: Upgrades Robbie. Busy: look at the top two cards of the Market Deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: The suit that week had a repeating pheasant on it. Asked where it came from, he said it was off the peg — and then, after a pause nobody filled, off the peg-asant.

cards.name: Robbie
cards.title: Editor
cards.text: Upgrades Robbie. At the start of your turn, the next card revealed in the Capital City does not affect you, and look at the top two cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: He is at the back of the hall at half past eleven with the notebook out, and the story runs whether or not anybody rang back.

cards.name: Robbie
cards.title: Editor-in-Chief
cards.text: Upgrades Robbie. A patient shift: 2 turns, 3 Supply. At the start of your turn, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck, put one of them to the bottom, and the next card revealed in the Capital City does not affect you.
cards.flavor: The paper is six sheets now and still comes out on a Thursday. Whatever the Capital City had lined up for the front of the display, Robbie has seen it, moved it, and made a joke about it that only he enjoyed.

cards.name: Cornelius
cards.title: FutureTech CEO
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy, and goes back to the city after three of your turns, where he may be hired again. At the start of your turn, Buildings cost you 3 less. When Cornelius becomes upright, every lot in the Capital City with a roof on it costs you 2 less.
cards.flavor: Forty minutes, three automatons and a folder. The schedule works, the roof went up for nothing, and the ward cannot now find the bit it agreed to in writing.

cards.name: FutureTech HQ
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, every one of your Characters who is not upright stands up.
cards.flavor: Glass to the fourth floor, a lobby you may walk through and two floors you may not, and a company that posts a record quarter in a year the bridge went. Cornelius will show you everything. He will show you the second floor last, and then the tour will be over.

cards.name: The Hospital
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 3 less Supply, and they come back upright.
cards.flavor: Pristine, quiet, and owned since the spring by FutureTech, which repainted the wards and kept every one of the staff. An animal who stops getting up goes in through those doors and comes out fit for a shift, which is more than the borough could say a year ago.

cards.name: The FutureTech Store
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply for each Building you have raised, up to 4.
cards.flavor: Everything in the window is a month old and everything behind the counter is a fortnight. Jim is in the queue on launch day whatever it is, and the whole street is richer for the queue.

cards.name: Starfish Coffee
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: The land's coffee chain, the borough's branch, and not an animal behind the counter: three automatons, a menu board that changes itself, and a FutureTech name on the receipt in very small print. The queue moves faster than anywhere else in town.

cards.name: The Ice Cream Shop
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, one of your opponent's Characters is put back to work. This does not happen again until your turn after next.
cards.flavor: Owned by an old Raccoon who retired to the arctic and never quite got round to selling it, and run to the inch by four teenagers who have never met him. Half the other town is in the queue on a warm afternoon and none of them are at work.

cards.name: The Clinic
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, your recruits that upgrade a Character you control cost 2 less this turn.
cards.flavor: Two rooms, a scrubbed floor and a coral tank in the waiting office that the babies of both boroughs will sit in front of for an hour. Whatever an animal came in unable to do, they generally go out able to do it.

cards.name: Tax Day
cards.text: Requires a Commerce Character. Gain 1 Supply for each Character in your town, up to 8.
cards.flavor: One morning a year the whole borough queues at the assize office with a tin and a grievance, and one morning a year the ward is solvent. Peanut has the desk. Cindy has the room next door, for the grievances.

cards.name: FutureTech Release Day
cards.text: Requires a Science Character. Pay 2 Supply: search your deck for a card that says FutureTech, take it into your hand, and shuffle.
cards.flavor: The line starts at the store and goes past the coffee bar, which is FutureTech's too, and round to the HQ steps, which are FutureTech's as well. Jim is second. Jim is always second, and has never once explained who is first.

cards.name: Otter Time!
cards.text: Requires an Otter. Recruit any number of Otters from your hand for free, then pay 2 Supply to search your deck for an Otter, take it into your hand, and shuffle.
cards.flavor: It is not on any calendar and it is not anybody's idea. Somebody goes in off the ferry steps, and within the hour there is no otter in either borough doing the thing they were doing.

cards.name: Henrietta
cards.title: Front Desk Clerk
cards.text: When Henrietta is recruited, you may recruit a Rabbit costing 1 or less from your hand for free; if you do, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: She has the board updated before the ink on the posting is dry, and a full account of the posting animal's cousins before anybody has asked for one.

cards.name: Henrietta
cards.title: Placement Officer
cards.text: Upgrades Henrietta. Busy: you may recruit a Rabbit costing 3 or less from your hand for free; if you do, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: She works the whole room for a good posting — the warren, the cousins, the animal who is definitely ready to move on from the Gate Hut — and never once mentions that she is working it.

cards.name: Henrietta
cards.title: Head of Rabbit Recruitment
cards.text: Upgrades Henrietta. Busy: you may recruit a Rabbit from your hand for free; if you do, gain 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: The title is new and she gave it to herself, and nobody has argued, because when the good Rabbits are worth having Henrietta is on the warren telegraph until they are standing in your town, several stories the richer for the trip.

cards.name: The Casino Fundraiser
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors lose half their Supply, then both Mayors gain 4 Supply. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Table games in the Long Hall for one night, run for both boroughs by whoever the Capital City sends out, and the till comes out even by morning whatever went in.

cards.name: Balto
cards.title: Bench Owl
cards.text: When Balto is recruited, your Owl and Badger Characters' next shift each produces 1 extra Supply.
cards.flavor: A knock at three in the morning and a wobbling table leg, and Balto is already out the door with the right chisel.

cards.name: Balto
cards.title: Cabinetmaker
cards.text: Upgrades Balto. Busy: your Owl and Badger Characters' next shift each produces 1 extra Supply.
cards.flavor: Fifty years of dovetails, and he still will not say which joint he is proudest of, only that it is somewhere in the Open Mic Room and nobody has noticed it yet.

cards.name: Balto
cards.title: Shopkeeper
cards.text: Upgrades Balto. When Balto completes a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: He found, to his mild surprise, that he could charge for some of it. He still gives half of it away first and charges for what is left.

cards.name: Balto
cards.title: Furniture Craftsman
cards.text: Upgrades Balto. Busy: your Owl and Badger Characters' next shift each produces 1 extra Supply.
cards.flavor: Half the good chairs in either borough go under his name now, and none of them were ever formally sold — a neighbor mentioned a bad back, and a chair turned up.

cards.name: Balto
cards.title: Guild Furniture Broker
cards.text: Upgrades Balto. At the start of your turn, your Owl and Badger Characters' next shift each produces 2 extra Supply, and gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Fifty years in, and he still does the neighbor first and the counter second, in that order, every single night, whatever the guild's ledger would prefer.

cards.name: Fingers
cards.title: Rooftop Runner
cards.text: When Fingers is recruited, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: He was sent for and was already there. Ask how and you get the shrug.

cards.name: Fingers
cards.title: Chimney Sweep
cards.text: Upgrades Fingers. Busy: look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: Up one flue and down the next, and he comes out the other end with a fair idea of what the Capital City has coming before it has finished sweeping its own chimney.

cards.name: Fingers
cards.title: Root-Cellar Diver
cards.text: Upgrades Fingers. Busy: take a card out of the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Under the grange, past a door nobody left unlocked, and up again with exactly the thing that was wanted. The grange has stopped asking which door.

cards.name: Fingers
cards.title: Master Locksmith
cards.text: Upgrades Fingers. Busy, pay 3 Supply: search your deck for a Fingers card, take it into your hand, then shuffle.
cards.flavor: He picked the ward court's lock for practice once, put everything back exactly as it was, and left a note saying so. The note is still filed under Ned's unsigned column.

cards.name: Fingers
cards.title: The One Who Gets In
cards.text: Upgrades Fingers. Busy: you may recruit another Fingers card from your hand for free, cheaper or dearer than this one — for Fingers alone, the ladder runs both ways.
cards.flavor: Every other animal in the First Boroughs can only ever move up. Fingers has never once seen why that should apply to him.

cards.name: Raccoon Family Reunion
cards.text: Requires a Raccoon. Search your deck for any number of Raccoons and recruit any number of Raccoons from your hand and deck, as many as your town has room for, then every animal in your town becomes unemployed.
cards.flavor: Every cousin Fingers ever vouched for, and several nobody can place, in one town on one afternoon. By evening the board is bare, the Hiring Hall has no idea what happened, and nobody minds even slightly.

cards.name: Edwina
cards.title: Cheese Counter Girl
cards.text: Busy: your opponent discards a card.
cards.flavor: She pops up from behind the till at exactly the moment a customer has forgotten she is small enough to be behind it.

cards.name: Edwina
cards.title: Cheese Stall Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Edwina. When Edwina is recruited, your opponent discards a card.
cards.flavor: Market day, a full trestle, and Edwina somewhere underneath it, waiting for the one customer who has been rude about her prices.

cards.name: Edwina
cards.title: Cheese Cellar Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Edwina. Busy: your opponent discards a card; you may then pay 2 Supply to make them discard a second.
cards.flavor: She knows the cellar's every shelf and every gap behind it, which is a lot of places for a Mouse who has decided today is your day to be waiting.

cards.name: Edwina
cards.title: Cheese Merchant
cards.text: Upgrades Edwina. Busy: your opponent discards a card; you may then pay 2 Supply to make them discard 2 more.
cards.flavor: She has opinions about the supplier and a memory for every short delivery, and the Counting House has learned to simply believe her the first time.

cards.name: Friendship Festival
cards.text: Requires a Cat and a Mouse. Recruit any number of Cats and Mice from your hand for free, matched pair for pair, then pay 2 Supply to search your deck for one Cat and one Mouse, take them into your hand, and shuffle.
cards.flavor: The borough decided some years ago that a Cat and a Mouse ought to have one day a year they are told to get along, and has been quietly pleased ever since at how often it works.

cards.name: Eustace
cards.title: Socialite
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. When Eustace is recruited, your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: He does nothing you could point to and somehow the whole afternoon is over before you meant it to be, and everybody in the room is charmed rather than annoyed about it.

cards.name: Eustace's Ball
cards.text: Requires Eustace. Your Cats and Badgers advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: Eustace throws one for no occasion anybody can name, the Cats leave early because they please and the Badgers leave early because for once nothing needs finishing, and both are back at work sooner than the evening should have allowed.

cards.name: Cynthia
cards.title: Junior Lab Assistant
cards.text: When Cynthia completes a shift, take a Science token.
cards.flavor: She starts the jar on her first day and has never once explained what the tokens are for, mostly because she has not decided yet.

cards.name: Cynthia
cards.title: Paint-Drying Researcher
cards.text: Upgrades Cynthia. When Cynthia completes a shift, take 2 Science tokens.
cards.flavor: The desk caught fire three feet away and she did not notice, because the paint was the more interesting variable. The desk was replaced within the week; the story was not.

cards.name: Cynthia
cards.title: Combustion Theorist
cards.text: Upgrades Cynthia. Busy: spend 2 Science tokens to gain 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: The desk fire taught her something after all, eventually, several open mic nights later: the jar is worth cashing in, not just keeping.

cards.name: Cynthia
cards.title: Head of the Absorption Wing
cards.text: Upgrades Cynthia. At the start of your turn, take a Science token. Busy: spend 3 Science tokens to gain 6 Supply.
cards.flavor: Nobody at the Science hall has ever explained what the Absorption Wing studies. Cynthia has, several times, at length, and nobody has followed any of it.

cards.name: The Science Lab
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may recruit a Science Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free.
cards.flavor: FutureTech funds it quietly, a floor below the Hospital's books and two above where anybody is allowed to ask questions, and the borough's own Science hall has stopped minding where the money comes from.

cards.name: The Grocery Store
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Nothing about it is remarkable, which is rather the point: bread, milk, a till that adds up, and a queue that never once talks about the Capital City.

cards.name: Nancy
cards.title: Temp Agency Runner
cards.text: When Nancy is recruited, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: She has somebody on their feet again before the ink on the Unemployment slip is dry, nails clicking on the counter the whole time she is doing it.

cards.name: Nancy
cards.title: Temp Agency Manager
cards.text: Upgrades Nancy. Busy: you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: She runs the whole board herself now, and the Hiring Hall's longer-serving clerks have learned better than to argue with her about the rate twice.

cards.name: The Mayor's Conference
