cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors search their deck for a Character and hire them, entering Busy, and nobody's Characters advance at the next Ready. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Both Mayors are called to the Capital City on the same short notice, and both come home with somebody new and no time yet to put them properly to work.

newStudies.name: Food
newStudies.blurb: Feeding the town: counters, kitchens, carts and the café. Where Commerce counts the money and Agriculture grows the crop, Food is the animal who hands it over and knows everyone's order.

newStudies.name: Entertainment
newStudies.blurb: The town's evenings: stages, bands, open mic nights, the halls people fill when the shift is over. Civics keeps the town working and Entertainment keeps it worth working for.

townCards.note: The market side of the shelf: Buildings, Events, Market cards, Disruptions and the nine Statues that give the cast, species and studies something to play with. These cards belong to no character entry — a Building is not somebody's backstory — which is why they are listed here. Town Buildings have no art yet: `wantedArt` lists what each one should show, so the illustrations can be commissioned in one batch.

wantedArt.what: A long allotment strip in late summer, four generations of tools against the fence, one rabbit writing in a notebook at the end of it.
wantedArt.painted: Painted. mk_tb_allotment_strip → the makerfield atlas, tile 15. (A Maker atlas tile wins over anything on the card itself — `explicitArt` in src/ui/painted-art.js reads MAKER_ART_TILES first — so a card that still carries the older shared `art` shows the commissioned scene.)

wantedArt.what: A cellar under a weights office: salt sacks, lamp oil, candle stock and a shelf of small coin, everything squared away and plainly never touched.

townCards.wantedArtNote: Audited 2026-09-14: every wish on this list has since been painted — the eight Maker atlases (docs/MAKER_ATLAS_ART.md) cover all fourteen Town Buildings and Capital City Buildings, and each entry now carries a `painted` line naming the tile that answers it. They are kept rather than deleted because the wish is what the tile was painted from.

tokens.note: The token shelf. A token is a marker a Mayor holds beside their Supply — never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck — and each kind is declared by one card here: ten species, eight studies, and one for Buildings. The rules are spec/game.json `tokens`; the engine holds the counts in `player.tokens` and gives, spends and reads them with `gainToken`, `spendToken` and the `tokensAtLeast` condition. The counter was built before any card spent one, deliberately, because tokens are the obvious answer to a whole family of cards the collection keeps reaching for — 'your Rabbits are worth something to each other', 'Food pays for Food', 'the town has built before and it shows' — and every one of those cards wants the same counter underneath it. Those three cards now exist and they are the Warren Muster, the Ovens' Account and the Surveyor's Table: one counter, three cards, none of them inventing their own. Each spends what another card gives — the Chit Tin and the two Founders' cards hand out Building chits, the Harvest Fair a Food chit, the Warren Muster its own first Rabbit — and a price a town cannot meet is not paid at all, so a short holding spends nothing and the card's other half still happens.

wantedArt.what: One sheet of ten round wooden chits, each stamped with a species in the borough's own hand — not a portrait but a maker's mark: ears, a tail, a set of quills. Worn edges; these have been in pockets.
One sheet of eight square chits carrying the study icons already used on the card faces, struck in the same wood and the same hand as the species sheet.
A single surveyor's chit, larger than the rest and stamped with a roofline, lying on the corner of a plan with a tin of them behind it.

marketDecks.name: The Grand Exchange
marketDecks.blurb: The whole catalogue under one roof: every lot the borough has ever put up, every Ordinance the Capital City can post, every kind of weather, and a dozen virtues to raise nine of. The market to play to meet the collection — no two games deal the same city.

marketDecks.name: The Hard Frost
marketDecks.blurb: The winter the Grain Exchange shut and the assessors came round anyway: a Capital City that takes animals off your board, posts an Ordinance about it, and then puts the monuments up by a third.

marketDecks.name: The Open Hiring
marketDecks.blurb: The board is full, the hall is open and everything on it is somebody looking for work or a roof looking for a crew. The bidding here is over labour rather than weather, and a town that can pay leaves with a bigger town.

marketDecks.name: Guild Row
marketDecks.blurb: A street of counters, tins and subscriptions: chits handed out by the guild, Supply put by for the year you need it, and a discount for anyone who turns up early. The slow, rich Capital City — nothing here hits you, and everything here compounds.

needsArt.note: Cards that are written, playable and not yet painted. A card lands here the moment it is written without `art`, and leaves it the moment a scene is commissioned — src/ui/painted-art.js for a bundled painting, or an `art` block on the card for an atlas tile. docs/NeedsArt.md is generated from this list and is the version an illustrator reads: it carries the card, the character behind it and the story the scene has to tell. The art tests read this list and let a card through unpainted only while it is on it, so nothing is quietly forgotten.
